states.name: Texas
states.agency: Railroad Commission of Texas
states.basis: issue date

source.name: Drilling Permit Master and Trailer (application type 01, new drill)

states.cadence: publishes daily; this report's series is rebuilt by hand
states.note: The monthly files are rebuilt by hand; the Daily report holds the newest days.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.agency: Oklahoma Corporation Commission
states.basis: approval date

source.name: Intents to drill (master workbook and the daily file)

states.cadence: publishes daily; this report refreshes weekly

states.name: New Mexico
states.agency: Oil Conservation Division
states.basis: spud date

source.name: Public well layer (Wells_Public)

states.cadence: publishes daily; this report refreshes weekly
states.note: Spud dates arrive about two months late, so the series ends two months back.

states.name: Federal offshore
states.agency: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement
states.basis: spud date

source.name: Borehole data (the weekly all-releasable file)

states.cadence: publishes weekly; this report refreshes weekly
states.note: About 45 wells a year; spud dates arrive late. The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) publishes the file.

states.name: Federal onshore (BLM)
states.agency: Bureau of Land Management
states.basis: approval date (APDs approved)

source.name: Application for Permit to Drill Status Report (monthly PDF, by BLM state office)

states.cadence: monthly
states.note: APDs (applications for permit to drill) approved by BLM state office, new drills and re-entries together, federal and tribal lands together; an office is not a state (New Mexico's covers Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas). Shown on its own and never added to the states, which permit most of the same wells. The series starts in 2022-12: the BLM's monthly reports run from April 2021, but the October and November 2022 reports were never linked on its page, so the unbroken run starts there.

states.name: Alabama
states.agency: State Oil and Gas Board of Alabama
states.basis: permit date (the day the permit was issued)

source.name: OGB Online Map, Wells layer (permit date)

states.cadence: as permits are issued (the Board states no schedule)
operators: LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT INC.
states.note: Permits counted by their permit date. A new well is a permit that takes the next number in the Board's sequence, nearly all coal bed methane in the Black Warrior Basin (about 30 a year, so a month is often zero); permits on wells numbered earlier (re-permits, deepenings, re-entries, amendments: the layer does not say which) are 'other filings', and injection, disposal and water-source permits are their own band. Cancelled permits drop out of the layer (about one number in seven was missing from 2023 to 2026), so a count can be a little short.

states.name: Alaska
states.agency: Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (AOGCC)
states.basis: approval date

source.name: AOGCC Data Miner: Well Work Dates and Wells (the 'ZIP (All Data)' downloads)

states.cadence: each weekday (the Data Miner is refreshed every weekday evening)
states.note: Permits to Drill approved by the Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission, counted by the day each was approved. The Commission gives every sidetrack and every lateral leg of a well a permit of its own, so these are permits, and many are for existing wells: new wells are the original holes of Development and Exploratory class, injection and disposal the original holes of Service class, re-entries and sidetracks the sidetracks and laterals of existing wells, and other filings the stratigraphic test wells (drilled for information, not oil or gas). The file dates no recompletion or amendment, so those kinds are not available. The places are the Commission's areas, not boroughs.

states.name: Arizona
states.agency: Arizona Oil and Gas Conservation Commission
states.basis: spud date (the day drilling began)

source.name: Oil and Gas Wells layer (ArcGIS, the Commission's well map)

states.cadence: irregular (the Commission edits the layer as it updates its records; it states no schedule)
states.note: Wells counted by their spud date, not by permit: the Commission's layer has no approval or filing date. Arizona drills very few wells, and the recent ones are helium, not oil (the fluid split says so). Only wells with a Commission permit number count. The newest spud the layer records is June 2023; the months since are zeros because none is recorded (the permits issued since then are listed as permitted, planned, extended or expired), up to the layer's last edit on September 24, 2026. Re-entries, reworks and amendments are not told. Spud dates arrive late, so the last two months are left off.

states.name: Arkansas
states.agency: Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission
states.basis: week of issue (the weekly report of Form 2 permits)

source.name: Permit and Completion Reports (one workbook a week)

states.cadence: weekly (a report for each week ending Friday)
states.note: Every Form 2 drilling permit on the Commission's weekly reports (North and South Arkansas). A report names a week, not a day, so each week is counted in the month that holds most of its days. A report prints a purpose under a permit that is not an original application (renewal, amend or re-entry): a permit with none is counted as new, a renewal or amendment as an amendment, a re-entry as a re-entry. The list gives no well type, so disposal, brine-supply and carbon-storage wells are among the new ones, and no injection or rework band and no fluid can be told. A few permits are listed again with no purpose printed and are counted as listed. The permit-by-permit record starts with the report for the week ending January 4, 2019. Weeks with no report in the Commission's archive, so a month that holds one may be short: November 29, 2019, January 19, 2024, October 4, 2024, January 30, 2026, May 8, 2026.

states.name: California
states.agency: California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM)
states.basis: approval date (CalGEM's determination on the notice of intention, as a California day)

source.name: WellSTAR Notices map service, Approved Notice of Intention/Permit layer

states.cadence: daily (the layer is current to the day)
states.note: Approved notices of intention (permits to drill, rework or plug), by the day CalGEM approved them. The layer starts on November 14, 2024 (the first month is a part month), so the series begins there, not in 2019. New wells are New Drill notices; those for injection, disposal, steam or water flood, storage, observation and water-source wells are their own band. Reworks (recompletions and conversions together) and sidetracks and deepenings have their own bands; plugging, about two thirds of all notices, is 'other filings'. Amendments are not told. Canceled notices are left out. Almost no new-drill permit was approved in 2025 and several hundred in 2026, so the change from the year before reflects what CalGEM approved, not necessarily what was drilled. 'Oil & Gas' is one CalGEM well type (shown as both); cyclic steam wells count as oil.

states.name: Colorado
states.agency: Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission (ECMC)
states.basis: spud date (the best spud date COGIS holds: the operator's notice of spud, then the date on the completion report)

source.name: ECMC Wells (API Spots) map service, spud date

states.cadence: daily (the layer is rebuilt every day)
operators: KERR MCGEE OIL & GAS ONSHORE LP
states.note: Wells spudded, by the spud date COGIS holds for each well (the operator's notice of spud, replaced by the actual date once the completion report is filed). Colorado approves roughly 800 to 1,100 drilling permits a year but publishes no file of the day each was approved: its search of approved permits holds only the last 12 months, so wells spudded is the series that can be told back to 2019, and it is not a count of permits. A well counts once, on its first spud date; the last month is left off. New wells are oil, gas, coal bed methane and dry-hole wells and wells not yet given a class; COGIS sets the class when the completion is reported, so most of the last year's wells read as fluid unknown, not as oil. Injection is disposal, enhanced-recovery and gas-storage wells; other wells are helium, CO2, domestic, observation and stratigraphic wells. Re-entries, recompletions and amendments are not told. The operator is the one on record today. Checked against the Commission's own well-starts table for 2023 to 2025.

states.name: Florida
states.agency: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Oil and Gas Program
states.basis: issue date (the day the final permit was signed)

source.name: Oil and Gas Permit Database (workbook, WELLS tab, issue date)

states.cadence: quarterly or as needed (the Department's words)
states.note: Permits counted by the date the Department signed them, from its own database, last saved September 8, 2026. Florida issues very few: the newest permit in the database was signed March 4, 2020, and months after it are zeros as the Department records them (applications still pending or denied carry no issue date and are not counted). A permit number with a letter (553A) is a modification of an earlier permit and counts as an amendment; the permit form records no well type, so injection and disposal permits cannot be told apart.

states.name: Idaho
states.agency: Idaho Department of Lands, Oil and Gas Conservation Commission
states.basis: approval date

source.name: Well and Facilities Files (one page per well, with its Permit to Drill)

states.cadence: irregular (a permit is posted within days of its approval)
operators: SNAKE RIVER OIL AND GAS LLC
states.note: Idaho approves very few: 8 permits to drill from January 2019 to September 2026, the newest on May 22, 2026, so a month with none is a real zero. Permits to drill, by the day the Commission approved each one: the date at the start of the Permit to Drill file linked from each well's page on its Well and Facilities Files list, checked against the signed permits and the Commission's quarterly counts. Two permits whose posted file is an amended version are counted at their first approval. Amendments, well treatments, seismic and injection permits are not available as dated records, and a permit that expired before a well was drilled has no page. Pages are posted within days to two weeks of approval, so the last 30 days are not shown. The list page was last edited June 4, 2026.

states.name: Illinois
states.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, Oil and Gas Resource Management (data from the Illinois State Geological Survey)
states.basis: permit date (the day the permit to drill was issued)

source.name: ILOIL Wells layer of the Illinois State Geological Survey (a permit date for every well)

states.cadence: weekly
states.note: Wells that received a permit to drill, by the day the permit was issued: oil, gas, coal-mine methane and injection wells together, because the survey's layer records the kind of well only once it is drilled (kinds of permits are not available). A permit to convert, deepen or renew an existing well adds no row (a conversion to injection was mostly missing in a check against the agency's weekly log). The layer runs about two months behind the agency's weekly permit log, so the series ends before the other states'.

states.name: Indiana
states.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Reclamation (Oil and Gas)
states.basis: issue date (the day the permit was issued)

source.name: Weekly Permits Listing (one PDF a week)

states.cadence: weekly (a list for each week ending Friday)
states.note: Every permit on the Division's weekly lists, by the day it was issued: new wells (oil, gas and coal bed methane), enhanced recovery and other service wells, deepenings, conversions, and modifications, renewals and changes of operator; test wells are other filings. The lists start in January 2020; a week with no permit has a list that says so, so a quiet month is a real zero. Two defects in the Division's own files leave a few permits out: its index points two weeks of July 2023 at one file (its monthly report counts two permits more than the lists for that month), and one PDF (the week ending September 2, 2022) prints three permits on top of each other, so two are not read. The last 14 months are read again each week, since a list may be corrected after release.

states.name: Kansas
states.agency: Kansas Corporation Commission, Conservation Division (through the Kansas Geological Survey's well database)
states.basis: permit date (approved notice of intent to drill)

source.name: KGS Oil and Gas Wells layer (permit date)

states.cadence: nightly (the KGS rebuilds the layer each night)
states.note: Notices of intent to drill the KCC approved, counted by the permit date in the KGS well layer (rows of the last days already read 'Approved Intent to Drill', so it is the approval date; the KGS does not say so). The layer has no work type: kinds come from the well type and the API number's suffix. New wells are oil, gas, coal bed methane, dry-hole and lost-hole permits on a new API number (a dry hole is a new well found dry); injection is enhanced-recovery (waterflood), saltwater-disposal and other injection or storage wells; re-entries are permits on an existing well's API number (a suffix such as -0001, which the KGS calls a workover code, also when the well is re-entered to inject); other filings are cathodic-protection boreholes (about 100 a year), water, stratigraphic and observation holes. Recompletions and amendments are not told. Permits whose API number was cancelled are left out. A well keeps one permit date, so a permit renewed on the same API number replaces the earlier date. The fluid is the well type the KGS holds today (a hole found dry reads unknown).

states.name: Kentucky
states.agency: Kentucky Division of Oil and Gas
states.basis: issue date

source.name: Weekly Permit Lists (one workbook a week)

states.cadence: weekly
states.note: Permits to drill, deepen, reopen or convert a well, by the day each was issued, from the Division's weekly lists (a workbook for each week ending on a Friday). A permit on two lists counts once. Injection, disposal, storage, water supply and test wells are told from the well type on the permit, and the fluid split is that type; reworks are conversions to injection, the only kind the lists carry; the lists have no amendments (shown as not available). The lists omit about 1% of permits (checked against the Geological Survey's well file in October 2026), so a month can be a little low. A month is shown once the lists reach its last day.

states.name: Louisiana
states.agency: Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy, Office of Conservation
states.basis: permit date (the day the permit was issued)

source.name: SONRIS GIS, Oil/Gas Wells layer of the Office of Conservation (permit date)

states.cadence: as permits are entered (the Office states no schedule)
operators: GRAYROCK ENERGY IV OPERATING COMPANY LLC
states.note: Permits counted by their permit date, one per well serial number. New wells are every permit in the oil and gas series: the layer cannot tell a new drill from a re-permit or a redrill, and a permit that later expired unspent stays counted. Injection and disposal permits (mostly aquifer-remediation and salt-water wells, numbered in the Office's own series) are their own band; its numbered orphan-well entries are 'other filings'. Re-entries, reworks and amendments are not told. Oil or gas is the product recorded for the well now, so a permit not yet drilled, dry or expired shows as not recorded.

states.name: Michigan
states.agency: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), Oil, Gas, and Minerals Division
states.basis: permit date (the layer's PermitDate, read as the day the permit was issued)

source.name: Oil, Gas, and Mineral Well Surface Hole Locations (EGLE open data map service, GrmdOpenData layer 10)

states.cadence: not stated by EGLE
states.note: Permits by the layer's PermitDate, read as the issue date (EGLE's documentation of the layer could not be read, so that is not confirmed). One record per well bore; a permit on two records is counted once. The layer has no work type: a sidetrack bore is told by its sidetrack number and counted under Re-entries and sidetracks, but re-entries, deepenings and reworks cannot be told, and amendments are not records, so they are not available. New wells are locations, oil and gas wells and dry holes (the well's current type): their fluid is known only for the producers, the rest are unknown. Lost holes are under Other filings; terminated permits are counted. Michigan issues about 30 to 70 permits a year, so a month is noisy.

states.name: Mississippi
states.agency: Mississippi State Oil and Gas Board
states.basis: approval date

source.name: Permit Search report

states.cadence: as permits are approved (the Board states no schedule)
states.note: Permits to drill, by the day the Board approved them, from its Permit Search report (the register of every permit it issues). New wells are original permits to drill an oil, gas, test or dry hole. Original permits for injection, disposal, gas or hydrogen storage and monitor wells count as injection (the well's type in the Board's well list decides). A re-entry is not told apart from a new drill. Reworks are workover, conversion and dual or triple completion permits; amendments are changes of operator, one permit per well, so one sale of many wells is a spike; other filings are H2S and pit permits. Counties and operators are those of the new wells. Fluid is the well's type in the well list: a well that came up dry is a dry hole there and counts as unknown. For each closed year the new and injection permits, less monitor wells, agree with the Board's own yearly Permits to Drill sheet to within a few permits (a run refuses to write if they differ by more). A month counts once it ended two weeks ago.

states.name: Montana
states.agency: Montana Board of Oil and Gas Conservation (Department of Natural Resources and Conservation)
states.basis: approval date (the day the Board approved the permit)

source.name: Dataminer, Well History (every event on every well, with the day it was approved)

states.cadence: as the Board enters approvals (it also posts a weekly activity letter, dated each Friday)
states.note: Every permit the Board's well history shows, by the day it was approved: permits to drill (vertical and horizontal), injection, disposal and storage wells, re-entries and re-drills of existing wells, and, as amendments, re-issued permits (a lapsed permit approved again for the same location) and permit modifications. Workovers and recompletions are filed on notices, not permits, so those bands are not available. Checked against the Board's annual reviews: their counts of wells permitted (new vertical and horizontal wells and re-entries of abandoned wells) and of re-issued permits match this file for 2019 to 2023, and for 2024 the review counts one more well permitted. A well's type and its operator are the Board's record today. The newest month is shown a week after it ends.

states.name: Nebraska
states.agency: Nebraska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission
states.basis: permit date (as listed by the Commission)

source.name: Drilling Permits (a list of permitted wells for each year), Data and Publications page

states.cadence: yearly (a year's list is posted after the year closes)
states.note: Every permit on the Commission's yearly lists of permitted wells, by the date it is listed under. The Commission posts a year's list after the year closes (2025's in March 2026), so these figures end with the newest closed year and a month with no permit is a real zero. The lists name no type of well: a permit is a re-entry when its API number says the well is an old one (the Commission prints OWWO), a disposal or injection well when the well is named SWD, WIW or the like, and a new well otherwise (two test wells for carbon storage are among them, as in the Commission's own totals). A well whose permit lapsed and was issued again counts each time. Amendments and recompletions are not on the lists, and the lists do not say oil from gas.

states.name: Nevada
states.agency: Nevada Division of Minerals
states.basis: approval date

source.name: Permits and Permit Notices (Oil and Gas page)

states.cadence: irregular
states.note: Permits to drill an oil or gas well, by the approval date in each permit's title on the Division of Minerals' Permits page, which lists the current year and the five before it (older months are kept from the earlier file). Nevada approves only a few a year, so a month with none is a real zero. The page names no well type, county or operator apart from the title's free text, so only new-well permits are counted and no county or operator is shown. The page is updated by hand: the last 30 days are not shown.

states.name: New York
states.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, Division of Mineral Resources
states.basis: issue date (the day the permit to drill was issued)

source.name: Oil and gas wells (wellDOS.zip: wellspublic.csv), updated every weekday night

states.cadence: nightly, Monday to Friday
states.note: Permits to drill by the day issued, one per well bore. The file has no work type: a sidetrack bore is told by its sidetrack code and counted under Re-entries and sidetracks, but a permit to deepen, re-enter, plug back or convert an existing well is not a row of its own, so those and amendments are not available. A further completion of an existing hole, stratigraphic test wells and permits with no type listed are under Other filings. Permits later expired, transferred or voided are counted. New York issues tens of permits a year, so a month is noisy; the file is rewritten nightly and a past month can move.

states.name: North Dakota
states.agency: North Dakota Industrial Commission, Oil and Gas Division
states.basis: spud date (the day drilling began)

source.name: Oil and Gas Division GIS, Wells layer (spud date)

states.cadence: as wells are reported (the Division's 2022 notice says hourly; not verified)
operators: BURLINGTON RESOURCES OIL & GAS COMPANY LP
states.note: Wells counted by their spud date, not by permit approval: the Division publishes approval dates only in daily PDF reports. New wells are the Division's oil and gas wells (it does not separate oil from gas) and the wells it still holds confidential, whose type is not shown (39% of the last 12 months' wells; they are in the oil counties and are counted as new, so a disposal well among them would make new a little high and injection a little low); injection and disposal wells are their own band; stratigraphic tests are 'other filings'. Re-entries, reworks and amendments are not told. Spud dates arrive late, so the last two months are left off.

states.name: Ohio
states.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management
states.basis: issue date (the day the permit was issued)

source.name: Permit and Plug List (Oil & Gas Well Database, Excel export of the Permit list)

states.cadence: live database, current to the day each permit is issued (read weekly here)
operators: HOCKING HILLS ENERGY AND WELL SERVICE LLC
states.note: Permits issued, by the day each was issued, from the Division's Permit and Plug List (Oil & Gas Well Database), the Permit list, which leaves out permits to plug a well. A permit to drill a new well (horizontal or vertical) is a new well, unless its well type is gas storage, a test hole, salt water or solution mining; permits to deepen a well, to reopen one and to plug back and drill again are re-entries; plain plug-backs and conversions are reworks; a re-issued permit, a revised location and a revised unit are amendments (the same well counted again). The Division's own count of permits to drill includes the deepenings and re-issues, so it is higher than the new wells here. The list does not say whether a well is oil or gas (its well type is oil and gas for nearly every well), so the fluid split is not available. The export lists some applications twice; each is counted once. A month is shown once a permit has been issued after it.

states.name: Oregon
states.agency: Oregon Department of Geology and Mineral Industries (DOGAMI)
states.basis: application date (the file has no approval date)

source.name: Oil & Gas Permits Spreadsheet (DOGAMI, .xls, updated by hand)

states.cadence: irregular (a few times a year)
states.note: Oregon permits only a few oil and gas wells a year, almost all gas, gas-storage and observation wells in the Mist field (Columbia County). Counted by the day an application was filed: DOGAMI's file has no approval date, no work type and no fluid. A permit number filed again on a later date is an amendment (a renewal: a permit lasts a year). The newest application in the file is dated 2025-12-12; the file is dated 2026-01-26 and DOGAMI updates it by hand. 3 applications still waiting (status Application) have no date in the file and are not counted.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Office of Oil and Gas Management
states.basis: permit date (the day DEP issued the well's drilling permit)

source.name: DEP Oil and Gas Mapping Application, Oil and Gas Wells All layer (permit date)

states.cadence: daily (the layer is current to a day or two)
states.note: Permits to drill a well, by the day DEP issued them (the layer has one row per well). Permits that expired unused or whose well the operator reported not drilled stay in the count: DEP issued them. Most are gas wells, many of them shale wells. Storage, injection, disposal and observation wells are their own band, a handful in six years. Re-drills, deepenings, alterations and changes of use are authorizations on existing wells that the layer does not show, so those bands are not told. The layer holds a few percent fewer wells than DEP's weekly Workload Report counts as permitted (555 against 576 for January 1 to October 23, 2026). The fluid is DEP's well type; an undetermined type or a dry hole is unknown.

states.name: South Dakota
states.agency: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Oil and Gas Program
states.basis: issue date (the day the permit to drill was issued)

source.name: Oil and gas wells export (Wells.xlsx in SDOILexport.zip, monthly)

states.cadence: monthly
states.note: South Dakota has issued very few permits: the newest in the program's export of 2026-10-01 is dated 2024-07-16, so every month since is a real zero, not a gap. Wells that received a permit to drill, by the day it was issued. Re-entries, reworks and extensions add no row (not available); the file is replaced whole each month, so earlier months can be revised.

states.name: Tennessee
states.agency: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of Mineral and Geologic Resources (Oil and Gas Program)
states.basis: permit date (the date the table records on each permit)

source.name: Oil and Gas Wells map layer (Oil_and_Gas2 MapServer, layer 0), the permit table behind the Oil and Gas Data Viewer

states.cadence: monthly (the Division's words for its oil and gas data)
states.note: Permits to drill an oil or gas well, by the permit date in the Division's table of every oil and gas well permit it has issued (its Oil and Gas Data Viewer and Map Viewer show the same table). The table has no type of permit, so only new wells are told. No permit number appears twice, so it reads as one row per permit to drill and amendments and transfers do not appear as rows. Permit numbers run in order without a gap. 77 percent of the permits since 2019 are for wells recorded as drilled and plugged dry. The fluid is the well's recorded purpose, which changes as it is drilled: a dry hole, a location not yet drilled and one abandoned have no fluid (unknown), so the newest months show more unknown than they will. Tennessee issues a few dozen permits a year, so a month with none is a real zero. The Division says it updates this data monthly, so the last 60 days before the read are not shown. The newest permit in the table is dated August 6, 2026.

states.name: Utah
states.agency: Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining
states.basis: approval date (APD approved)

source.name: Well History and Well Data download files (daily)

states.cadence: daily
states.note: Applications for Permit to Drill approved by the Division, by approval date: new wells, service wells (injection, disposal, storage, test), re-entries and deepenings, and a few potash, lithium, helium and carbon dioxide wells. Well type, county and operator are the well's current values, not those on the day of the permit. Recompletions, conversions and amendments are not available: the Division's file records them only as completed work.

states.name: Virginia
states.agency: Virginia Department of Energy (Virginia Energy), Division of Gas and Oil
states.basis: date drilling was completed (wells drilled; Virginia publishes no permit date)

source.name: DGO wells map service: Active, Plugged and Waste Disposal Wells (drilling completed date)

states.cadence: live map layer (no update time published)
states.note: Virginia Energy publishes no permit issue date by well, so this counts wells drilled, by the date their drilling was completed, never added to permits. Most are coalbed methane wells, most of them in Buchanan County. Wells drilled and since plugged are included; permits issued and not yet drilled are not. The newest well drilled in the layers is dated 2026-08-14; months run to 60 days before the read because a well's date arrives after the work. Operators are named only where they are companies.

states.name: West Virginia
states.agency: West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection, Office of Oil and Gas
states.basis: issue date, by week (Monday to Friday)

source.name: Weekly Permit Report (one list a week of the permit actions)

states.cadence: weekly (a report a few days after each week ends)
states.note: Permit actions from the Office's Weekly Permit Report: one list for each Monday-to-Friday week with no day by permit, so a week is counted in the month that holds most of its days. Issued permits are counted by type: new wells (New Drill, mostly horizontal 6A wells), re-entries (re-drill, drilling deeper), reworks (re-work, fracture, convert) and other (plugging permits, about half, and general or emergency permits). A modification of an issued permit is an amendment. Cancelled permits (counted when issued) and approved completion or plugging reports are left out. The reports hold no injection (UIC) permits, so no injection count is shown. The permit records no oil or gas, so no fluid is shown. The Office's map layer has exact dates but one row per well's latest permit, some of them twice, and no modifications; counted by permit number it agreed with these reports on new wells to within 2% when checked (Nov 2026), so the reports are the count. The series starts in February 2019, after the first report (the week of January 7). Weeks with no report (not counted): Dec 25, 2023, May 5, 2025, Dec 15, 2025.

states.name: Wyoming
states.agency: Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission
states.basis: approval date (APD approved)

source.name: Permits to Drill, Download Approved (one export a year)

states.cadence: daily
states.note: Applications for Permit to Drill approved by the Commission, by approval date: oil and gas wells, injection, disposal and monitor wells, and a few test holes. The file has no work type, so a re-entry, deepening or renewal is counted inside new wells; recompletions and amendments are not available. Well class and company are the permit's current values.

gaps.name: Missouri
gaps.agency: Missouri Department of Natural Resources, Missouri Geological Survey (staff to the State Oil and Gas Council), Rolla
gaps.why: Missouri publishes no current permit list: its wells map layer has no permit dated after August 2019, and the Geological Survey's wells list (updated August 2024) gives spud dates only, the newest in August 2023. It is a very small producer (41 wells spudded since 2019, 39 of them in Cass County).
